Early Letters: letters to your child, in your own words and voice.

Tell your child one thing about today. The first laugh, the long night, the song you made up in the car. It becomes a letter in your own words, with your voice kept beside it.

Years from now, your child can read it, and hear how you sounded when you said it.

IT STAYS IN YOUR WORDS
Your words are written down on your phone, and the app only fixes small slips, like an um, a repeat or a name spelled your way. It never adds a word. Every word we change is marked, and you can put any of them back. We never rewrite your words, shorten them or write for you. A word can be misheard, so have a quick read before you keep a letter. Letters you type stay as you typed them.

YOUR VOICE, KEPT
Every letter you speak keeps its recording, on your phone and in your iPhone's own backup if you use one. We never imitate your voice. Your original recording is always kept exactly as you made it.

READ TOGETHER AT BEDTIME
Open Read together and go through the book one letter at a time, oldest first. Listen to the letters you spoke, with the words on the screen. Typed letters are there too, for you to read aloud.

A MINUTE IS PLENTY
Some nights it's a sentence, some nights a long letter. Stuck for words? There's a question to start with. If today was quiet, tap "Not much today" and that's enough. Nothing keeps score.

A BOOK THAT GROWS BY MONTH
Each letter goes into your child's month of age, so the book reads in order. Expecting? Start before the birth, in a part of the book called Before You. Twins or more each get their own book.

NAMES SPELLED YOUR WAY
Add the names and home words you use, like a nickname or the name of a stuffed rabbit, so we spell them your way.

PRIVATE BY DEFAULT
Your letters and recordings are private. We never sell them, never use them for ads and never use them to train machine learning models. You sign in to keep your book. If you agree to sync, the words of your letters and your child's name and dates are kept on our servers so they reach a new phone. Recordings stay on the phone that made them. Keep any letter just for you, out of the book. Delete one and it waits in Recently deleted for 30 days.

REMINDERS, ONLY IF YOU WANT THEM
Reminders are off until you turn them on. You pick the days and the time, and none comes after 9:30 at night.

TAKE IT WITH YOU
Export your book any time, for free: your letters, your recordings and a PDF of the book.

IN ENGLISH
This version writes down letters spoken in English. The speech model is a one-time download, on Wi-Fi unless you turn on cellular data, 575 MB on most iPhones and smaller on some, and you choose when it starts. Until it is ready, your recordings are kept and the words follow.

PLUS
Your first two letters are free, so you can see how it feels. To keep adding letters, choose Plus: $4.99 a month with the first month free, or $49.99 a year with the first 2 months free. The free months are for people new to Plus. One plan covers every child's book and works with Family Sharing. A new letter past the free two waits until you decide. Every letter you have kept stays yours to read, play and export, with or without Plus.

Payment is charged to your Apple Account. Plus renews automatically unless you turn off renewal at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. Manage or cancel any time in your Apple Account settings.

rows.text: There are no ads. We never sell your data or share it with advertisers, and we never use your letters, recordings or photos to train models of any kind. Analytics never include letter text, recordings, photos, names or birthdays.
You can export your whole book, free, at any time, and delete your own letters, recordings or account whenever you like. The Privacy Policy has the full detail.

Your first two letters are free. After that, keeping another letter is part of Plus: ${plusPriceLine.monthly}, or ${plusPriceLine.annual}. Reading, playing your recordings and export are never locked away, with or without Plus.

${brand.name} is made and run by an independent maker in California, not a large company. Because it is published by an individual, the maker's legal name appears where the law asks for it: on the App Store listing and in the Terms and Privacy Policy.
If we ever plan to close, we will tell you at least 90 days ahead and keep export working the whole time.
Questions, ideas or a kind word are all welcome at hello@earlyletters.com. A person reads every message.
Most of what a family says to a small child is said once. ${brand.name} keeps those words, and the voice that said them.

Most of what a family says to a small child is said once. A joke at breakfast. A song made up in the car, with the words changed every time. Nani or Dadi telling the story of the night {child} was born, in the languages the family speaks, with every pause left in. It is said, it is heard, and the day moves on.

Photos keep what a day looked like, and they are wonderful at it. But a photo cannot tell {child} what you were thinking at the window that morning, or how you laughed before you finished the sentence. That part lives in words, and in a voice.
A book you fill by talking

Baby books ask a lot of tired people. Blanks to fill, firsts to date, a pen to find, a quiet hour that the early years rarely give. Many stop after a few pages, and that's nobody's failing. The format asks for time that is spent elsewhere, usually on the child.

Some parents find their own way. They write to an email address set up just for their child, or talk into a voice memo in the car, and plan to hand it all over one day. ${brand.name} is made for that instinct. Talk to {child} for a minute, and your words are kept as a letter in a book, filed under {child}'s age that month and signed with your name.

At the centre of everything is one promise: we never rewrite your words. We don't make them neater. We take out the ums and accidental repeats and spell your names your way, and we mark each fix. Every fix can be undone.
The way you say a thing is part of what you mean: the sentence you started twice, the way you always say the name. Smooth that out and it's easier to read, and less true.
You don't need to say it well. An ordinary day, said your way, is the one worth keeping.
A voice to come back to
Each letter also keeps its recording, so one day {child} can hear the words as well as read them: the pause before the punchline, the sleepy mumble at the end of a long night.
Read together plays a letter in your own voice, with the letter on the page. It is made for bedtime, and for hearing the same one twice.
There is no right amount to say. A minute is plenty. On a quiet day, Not much today is a complete answer. Nothing counts days or keeps score.
The book doesn't ask to be finished. It stays open for the next thing you want to tell {child}, whether that is tomorrow or next month.
A child is surrounded by voices. Both parents can write to {child}, each letter signed the way the family says it. From Mama. From Papa. From Amma.

Open ${brand.name}, tap Settings, then Your data, then Delete account.

The app shows what will happen to each book before you confirm, and offers Export everything first, free. If you have Plus, it reminds you how to cancel with Apple. To make sure it is you, it may ask for Face ID, your passcode or a code sent to your email, and then asks you to type to confirm.
Once you confirm, the app shows the date your account will be deleted, 30 days later, and we send a receipt by email.
If you cannot use the app, email hello@earlyletters.com from the address on your account, with Delete my account in the subject line.

Before we act, we confirm it is you. We send an email to that address with a link that confirms the request. The link opens a page in any web browser, so you do not need the app or an iPhone. The page shows the date your account will be deleted and how to cancel, and has one button, Delete my account.
If you signed in with Apple and chose Hide My Email, say so in your message and we will help you confirm it is you.
We reply within 10 business days. Once you confirm, your request follows the same steps and timeline as a deletion from the app.

Your letters, recordings and photos are removed from every book, including a book you share with a co-parent. That book stays with your co-parent, and we let them know that your letters are no longer in it. If you would like them to keep a copy, export yours first and share it.
A book where you are the only parent is deleted with everything in it.

Your profile, your family memberships and your account itself are deleted. We revoke your Sign in with Apple token, remove your Sign in with Google link, and delete the status of your Plus plan that the app reported to us. If you turned analytics on, we ask our analytics provider to delete the events sent under your analytics ID.

For 30 days after your request, your account is scheduled for deletion and you can change your mind. Sign in during that time and tap Cancel, and your letters and books come back. You can also still export.

After the 30 days, everything listed above is erased from our live database and storage within 31 days of your request, from our database backups within 38 days, and by our service providers within 45 days.
We email you when the request is made, if you cancel it, and when deletion is complete.
Any exports you made, and your phone's own backups, such as iCloud Backup, stay with you. Those are in your hands, not ours.

A few records stay, with no letters or recordings in them: a record of what you agreed to (3 years, without your name), activity records such as a letter was deleted (24 months, without your name) and support emails (2 years after your last one).

rows.text:
${brand.name} is a memory book that parents fill by talking. A parent speaks or types a short letter to their child. The app never rewrites what a person says. It makes only small marked fixes to the words it writes down (stray sounds, repeated words, a misheard name from the family's own word list, punctuation), and each fix can be put back. The birthday or due date a parent enters is used to file letters by month of age. This is not a health or medical service and gives no health advice.

SIGN-IN IS REQUIRED
An account keeps the words of a parent's letters with them on a new phone. Recordings stay on the phone that made them. Sign-in is Sign in with Apple, or a link and a 6-digit code sent by email. There are no passwords in the app.
Only if our sign-in service is down, the first screen also offers "${authCopy.outage.startLocal}". It is a stopgap for an outage, not a way to review the app, and the letters made there can be moved into an account later.

DEMO ACCOUNT (about 3 minutes)
Email: ${demoEmail}
Password: ${demoPassword}
The password opens the mailbox for that address, where the code arrives. It is not typed into the app. If you prefer, use Sign in with Apple with your own Apple Account instead.
1. On the first screen, tap Sign in with email.
2. Type the email address above in Email, then tap Send link.
3. Open the new email in that mailbox. Type its 6-digit code in Code, then tap Continue. Tapping the link on this iPhone also works.
4. Tap Agree and continue, then answer "Are you 18 or older?" with Yes.
5. Set up a book for a made-up child, for example Asha, and try a short letter by speaking or typing.
Sharing a book with a second parent is not needed to review the app.

DELETING THE ACCOUNT
Settings, Delete account. It shows what happens to each book, then asks you to type delete. The account is deleted 30 days later, and the deletion can be cancelled until then.

PLUS
The first two letters are free. Plus is asked for at Keep: keep two letters, then try to keep a third, or open Settings, Plan, to reach the Plus sheet. Please use a sandbox account. Nothing else is behind Plus, and every letter already kept stays readable, playable and exportable.

Contact: ${brand.support.email}
